title: Exact-Relation Coding: A Preregistered Test of Whether Discovered Fixed-Width GF(2)/Affine Structure Yields a Composed Lossless-Compression Advantage
notes: Frozen experiment state: git tag v1.1-final. Every quantity in the manuscript is generated from results/ledger.json (122 records) and verified by scripts/check_paper_numbers.py. The complete preregistered whole-file corpus was NOT executed: four of the twelve Silesia members and whole enwik8 / SDRBench / UCI exceeded the 8 GiB development machine and were run only at 256 KiB.
description:
A preregistered empirical study investigating whether discovered fixed-width GF(2)/affine structure yields a composed lossless-compression advantage. The mechanism produces large gains on deliberately structured data (planted GF(2) linear codes: composed gain up to +49.95 %, scaling with input size, not closed by paq8l or paq8px v216), but no non-prior-art natural file in the achieved coverage meets the preregistered per-file threshold (largest natural G_pct = +0.09 %, on a passthrough container). The complete preregistered corpus outcome is inconclusive because some whole-file runs exceeded available hardware; within the achieved coverage — 8 of 12 whole Silesia members, all 12 members plus enwik8 plus six SDRBench float32 fields plus a UCI telemetry file at 256 KiB, and a bounded bit-phase-offset detector extension — the result is a clean layered negative: exact structure is often present and discoverable, and on no tested file does it reduce the representation or survive composition. The mechanism is not novel (syndrome source coding; grammar-based compression; recent program-synthesis compression). The contribution is the accounting-complete codec with an independent shared-nothing verifier, the composed-gain evaluation discipline with a git-locked preregistered threshold, and the scoped empirical finding.

Artifact contents: the 17-page manuscript PDF and its Markdown/HTML source, generated results tables and figures, the machine-readable experiment ledger (122 records), the git-locked preregistration, the independent verifier, and one-command reproduction scripts. Canonical code repository and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/Xeloraa/deductive-coding (tag v1.1-final).
